results.claim: THEOREM 3.9: 'Definition 3.7 holds for every fixed k and every fixed admissible affine data' (log-averaged Chowla for all orders). The doc lists 1710.02112 among its three sources, calling it 'the odd-order paper', and assigns the all-orders case to arXiv:1809.02518; it also says 'All orders means every fixed k; the source does not claim uniformity in k.'
results.paper_quote: Theorem 1.1 (Odd order cases of the logarithmic Chowla conjecture): 'Let k >= 1 be an odd natural number, and let a_1,...,a_k,b_1,...,b_k be natural numbers. Then we have (1/log x) Sum_{n<=x} lambda(a_1 n+b_1)...lambda(a_k n+b_k)/n = o_{x->infinity}(1).' Abstract: 'we give a new and shorter proof of the odd order cases of the logarithmically averaged Chowla conjecture.' No all-k (even-order) result appears: 'we will only be dealing with odd values of k'.
results.doc_quote: 'Definition 3.7 holds for every fixed `k` and every fixed admissible affine data.' / 'also see [arXiv:1710.02112, J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux **30** (2018) 997-1015](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.02112) for the odd-order paper' / 'The all-orders case is attributed to the almost-all-scales structure theorem of arXiv:1809.02518.'
results.notes: Read full LaTeXML HTML of arXiv:1710.02112 (v1, 5 Oct 2017 — the only version; abs confirms no v2), plus abs. The doc's labelling of this paper as 'the odd-order paper' is accurate (Thm 1.1, k odd) and it does not attribute even k to it; but the headline claim it is cited under ('every fixed k') is broader than this paper, hence OVERSTATED. Numbering: 'THEOREM 3.9' is the archive's number, the paper's is Theorem 1.1; no version drift (single version). Metadata matches: Tao–Teräväinen, J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux 30(3) 997-1015 (2018). For odd k the paper needs no non-degeneracy condition (Remark 1.2), so 'admissible' is stricter than needed.
